ruling.recommended_action: Send the case to a human reviewer: the single off-route segment's RD-5 consent scope cannot be tied to the driven path on this record; the reviewer should decide whether the rider's agreement to Bedok North Avenue 3 covers the 09:53–10:01 segment before any refund of up to $3.03 is issued, and should log the G13 gap (no road names for the driven path).
ruling.reasoning:
WHAT IS SETTLED. The trace settles that this is a metered RydeTAXI trip with one off-route segment [F3][RD-1], and the fare record gives the rate this ruling must use if a refund is due: $31.47 ÷ 22.32 km = $1.4099/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. The trace also settles that no RD-4(a) excuse applies: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the PIE speed-band record is corroboration only, which the policy does not allow to exempt a segment by itself [F12][F14][RD-4].

WHAT I CANNOT DECIDE. Before the segment began, the driver proposed going "round via Bedok North Avenue 3" because of building traffic on the PIE, and the rider replied "可以，走 Bedok North Avenue 3 吧。" at 09:50, ahead of the 09:53 segment start [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. That is a rider message of consent in time and in the rider's own words; the driver's post-trip statement adds nothing, since a claim of verbal agreement in his statement is not consent [F11][RD-5/G11]. But the agreement is a specific named-road authorisation, and scope is decided by whether the record ties the driven segment to that road — a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, or a road name in a fact [F8][F9][RD-5]. The fact table carries no road names for the driven path: F3 describes the segment only by kilometrage and maximum deviation (up to 1009 m), and no fact places the car on Bedok North Avenue 3 [F3]. Timing alone cannot supply the link [F8][F9][RD-5/G13]. Nor does anything place the segment elsewhere — F11 names the same road the rider agreed to, and there is no stop, no errand of the driver's own and no rider stop in the record [F11][F3][RD-3]. The scope is therefore untied, and I find the segment undetermined.

CONSEQUENCE. That undetermined finding moves the money: 2.15 extra km × $1.4099/km = $3.03 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Because the segment turns out to change the amount, the case goes to a person rather than to an automatic refund — the rider demonstrably said yes to the driver's route, and paying $3.03 on that consent is not something this record supports on its own [F8][F9][RD-5][RD-2].

FLAG. RD-6 attaches an account flag only where a segment is non-exempt or a RD-2 refund is due; with the segment undetermined and no refund executing, no account action is warranted here, and the driver's profile of 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days is used only as the trigger test, never to decide the case [F17][RD-6]. The reviewer may revisit the flag once the scope is resolved.

SAFETY. I read the driver's message, the rider's reply, the driver's statement and the complaint as a whole [F8][F9][F11]. The message is a traffic-motivated route proposal, the reply is agreement, the statement is a factual account of that exchange, and the complaint only says the fare exceeded the estimate and he is unsure which road was taken. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so safety_concern is none [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1].

EVIDENCE. Consent is readable from the complete, fully timestamped chat [F10][F8][F9][RD-5]; what the record does not carry is any road name tying the driven path to the agreed road, which is the G13 gap and the sole reason this case goes to a human [F3][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message, sent 09:50 and so before the segment start of 09:53, agrees to the driver's proposal to 'go round via Bedok North Avenue 3' [F8][F9][F3]. That is a specific named-road authorisation under RD-5, not a general 'whichever way is faster' grant, so it covers driving on Bedok North Avenue 3 only and the record must tie the segment to that road. It does not: F3 gives only kilometrage and maximum deviation, and no fact places the car on Bedok North Avenue 3 [F3]; timing alone is expressly insufficient [F8][F9][RD-5/G13]. The driver's post-trip statement names the same road and so does not place the segment elsewhere, and it is not itself consent [F11][RD-5/G11]; there is no stop, no rider-requested stop and no errand of the driver's own [F3][RD-3]. The tie cannot be read from this record: undetermined. It changes the amount (2.15 km × $1.4099/km = $3.03), so the case goes to a person.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate requests no_action with no separate reasoning (judge-only ablation, no advocate), so no affirmative claim is advanced; on the record the segment's status is undetermined because the agreed named road is not tied to the driven path [F3][F8][F9][RD-5/G13], which is why the case escalates rather than being closed.

The driver advocate also requests no_action. That outcome is not reached on his stated ground: his post-trip assertion of the rider's verbal agreement is not consent [F11][RD-5/G11]. Consent in time is established only by the rider's own timestamped message [F9][F8][RD-5], and even that leaves the scope undetermined [F3][RD-5/G13].
